India.climate: El Niño can weaken the summer monsoon, raising the likelihood of below-average rainfall and hotter conditions. The Indian Ocean and other climate patterns also influence the outcome.
India.economy: Rain-fed crops and rural incomes are exposed to poor monsoon rainfall. Lower reservoir levels can put pressure on irrigation, hydropower, and food prices.
India.health: Heat exposure, water scarcity, and reduced food access can increase health risks. Disease patterns depend on local temperature, rainfall, and public-health conditions.
India.nature: Dry soils and water stress can affect crops, forests, and freshwater ecosystems.
India.action: Follow local monsoon outlooks, conserve water, and prepare heat-health plans.

Australia.climate: El Niño often brings reduced rainfall to eastern Australia, with warmer daytime temperatures and an earlier start to fire-weather conditions.
Australia.economy: Drought can reduce crop yields and pasture growth, raise livestock feed costs, and constrain water-dependent industries.
Australia.health: Heat and wildfire smoke can affect respiratory health. Drought can also increase mental-health pressures in rural communities.
Australia.nature: Reduced river flows, dry vegetation, and elevated fire risk put ecosystems under stress.
Australia.action: Monitor seasonal outlooks, review bushfire plans, and manage water supplies.

Indonesia.climate: El Niño commonly delays rains and increases dry-season drought risk across parts of Indonesia.
Indonesia.economy: Water stress can affect rice production, plantations, and hydropower. Fires and haze can disrupt transport and economic activity.
Indonesia.health: Smoke from forest and peat fires can increase respiratory illness; heat and water scarcity add pressure.
Indonesia.nature: Dry peatlands and forests become more vulnerable to fire and habitat loss.
Indonesia.action: Prepare for water shortages, monitor fire warnings, and limit smoke exposure.

Peru.climate: Eastern-Pacific El Niño events can bring unusually warm coastal water and heavy rainfall to northern coastal Peru. Effects differ elsewhere in the country.
Peru.economy: Flooding can damage transport and farms, while warmer ocean water can alter fisheries and fishmeal supply.
Peru.health: Flood injuries, disrupted care, and contaminated drinking water can increase health risks.
Peru.nature: Reduced upwelling changes marine nutrients and can displace fish populations.
Peru.action: Follow coastal flood alerts, protect drinking water, and prepare evacuation routes.

United States of America.climate: El Niño often favors wetter conditions across the southern US and warmer conditions in the north. Regional effects vary, and individual storms are not guaranteed.
United States of America.economy: Changes in winter storms affect agriculture, water supply, energy demand, and transport. Flood exposure can rise in some southern areas.
United States of America.health: Flooding and storms can cause injuries and interrupt access to care; warmer winters can shift local health exposures.
United States of America.nature: Rain and snowpack changes affect watersheds and habitats differently across the country.
United States of America.action: Use local seasonal forecasts and prepare for regional flood and storm hazards.

Brazil.climate: El Niño can favor drought and heat in parts of northern Brazil and wetter conditions in southern Brazil.
Brazil.economy: Regional drought and floods can affect agriculture, hydropower, and transport in different ways.
Brazil.health: Heat, smoke, and floods pose region-specific risks. Water and vector-borne disease patterns depend on local conditions.
Brazil.nature: Drier conditions can increase fire vulnerability in the Amazon, while southern ecosystems may face flooding.
Brazil.action: Check regional forecasts and prepare for the locally relevant drought or flood risk.

Kenya.climate: El Niño is often associated with wetter short rains in equatorial East Africa, although the Indian Ocean Dipole also plays an important role.
Kenya.economy: Rain can benefit crops and pasture, but excessive rainfall can damage farms, roads, and livelihoods.
Kenya.health: Flooding can contaminate water and disrupt health services. Some vector-borne disease risks can increase under suitable conditions.
Kenya.nature: Heavy rain can cause erosion and flooding, alongside improved vegetation growth.
Kenya.action: Monitor short-rains forecasts and prepare flood response and safe-water supplies.

South Africa.climate: El Niño often raises the risk of below-normal summer rainfall and warmer conditions in southern Africa.
South Africa.economy: Drought can affect maize production, livestock, water supplies, and agricultural incomes.
South Africa.health: Heat and food or water insecurity can increase health burdens, especially in vulnerable communities.
South Africa.nature: Low soil moisture and river flows can stress grasslands and freshwater habitats.
South Africa.action: Plan water conservation, monitor crop conditions, and prepare for heat.
